target_customer: Startups and SMBs in Latin America, mainly B2C sales and marketing teams, that sell through WhatsApp
problem: Businesses in Latin America run sales and support on WhatsApp but lacked no-code tools to follow up leads, automate messages and connect CRMs and payments.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription on top of the WhatsApp Business API
product_category: WhatsApp automation and conversational marketing platform

founders.name: Alfonso Lizarraga
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the only founder and describes him as looking for social problems to solve in LATAM through tech and product design.

technical_complexity.rationale: A no-code layer over the WhatsApp Business API with an inbox and flow builder is standard SaaS; the API itself was supplied by Meta partners.

defensibility.rationale: Many providers resold the same API; integrations and Spanish language support gave modest lock-in, and platform access depended on Meta.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large API and inbox vendors stayed in the market; Hilos was acquired by ActiveCampaign in April 2025, which wanted native WhatsApp automation.

market_need_then: WhatsApp is the main customer channel for many Latin American businesses; no dated spend data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Launch post framed the product as Zapier for WhatsApp

branding.brand_signature: Zapier for WhatsApp positioning in the 2022 launch post

brand_strength.rationale: Limited press beyond Latin American startup outlets and the acquisition coverage; a separate Hilos Inc footwear company exists.

outcome_analysis: Hilos joined YC S21 as a small team and was acquired by ActiveCampaign, announced April 2025, with the team joining and the technology folded into ActiveCampaign. The price and funding history are not verified. It reads as a modest strategic exit tied to demand for WhatsApp channels, but no factors are assigned because sources give no numbers.
notes: The YC slug is quid but the company is Hilos (hilos.io); a prior name is not documented, so no rebrand recorded. Funding aggregators conflict ($580K over 5 rounds on CB Insights, $990K on Startup-seeker, a $3M seed on Tryfundable) and none is confirmed by a press release, so no rounds are recorded. Competitor searches returned only current vendor guides, nothing dated near 2021, so the list is empty.
